direction: Discovery research in health — mechanistic understanding of disease
title: Dissecting the tissue-immune crosstalk that drives chronic inflammation into organ fibrosis
background: Chronic inflammation is a shared driver of progression to irreversible organ fibrosis across the lung, liver, kidney and heart, yet the mechanisms by which persistent immune activation is converted into a self-sustaining, matrix-depositing fibrotic programme remain poorly understood. Single-cell and spatial technologies have revealed remarkable heterogeneity of fibroblast and macrophage states, but a unifying, causal account of how tissue-resident stromal cells and infiltrating immune cells co-evolve over time to reach a fibrotic 'point of no return' is lacking. Establishing this mechanistic understanding is a prerequisite for stage-appropriate, tissue-agnostic anti-fibrotic strategies. This programme proposes an integrated, longitudinal and cross-organ investigation combining spatial multi-omics, lineage tracing, organoid/organ-on-chip perturbation and in vivo intervention to define the causal cellular circuits and molecular switches that commit chronically inflamed tissue to fibrosis.
challenges: Distinguishing causal drivers from bystander cell states: high-resolution atlases describe fibroblast/macrophage heterogeneity but do not establish which transitions are necessary and sufficient for fibrotic commitment

Capturing temporal dynamics and the fibrotic 'point of no return': most human data are cross-sectional snapshots; longitudinal, perturbable models are needed to identify reversible vs irreversible stages
Achieving cross-organ generalisability: identifying shared, tissue-agnostic immune-stromal circuits versus organ-specific mechanisms, to support therapies that transfer across fibrotic diseases
Bridging mechanism to intervention: translating identified molecular switches into testable, stage-appropriate intervention points while managing the risk of impairing normal wound healing

budget.note: Wellcome Discovery Awards have no fixed upper funding limit; the average award is ~£3.5M and applications above £5M undergo additional scrutiny. Duration may run from 3 to 8 years; ~7 years (84 months) used here as a representative figure. Budget must be fully justified against the proposed research.

eligibility: Established researchers with the experience to drive and lead a research programme, a track record of managing/training others, and a permanent, open-ended or long-term rolling contract. Applicants must be based in the UK, the Republic of Ireland, or low- and middle-income countries (excluding India and mainland China). An award may be held by an individual or a team of typically 2–8 applicants led by an established researcher.
requirements: Deliver discovery research that advances mechanistic understanding within Wellcome's health remit
Provide a Data Management Plan and make outputs openly available in line with Wellcome's open-access and open-data policies
Justify all requested costs against the scientific programme
constraints: The proposed research must fall within Wellcome's remit of discovery research that improves human life and health
Applications exceeding £5,000,000 are subject to additional scrutiny
Lead applicant and organisation must meet Wellcome's eligibility and location requirements
